title: Ops Resilience: Restoration Race
description: Grid secured. Now comes the hard part: restoring power to 200,000 homes and businesses without triggering another cascade failure. Every decision affects real people.
storyContext: Grid secured, but 200,000 homes still dark. Hospitals running on backup generators with maybe four hours of fuel. MRT stations on emergency lighting. The Minister just promised power by morning on national TV. One wrong move in the restoration and you overload the healthy grid — turning a partial blackout into a total one.

software-engineer.title: Program the Restoration Sequence
software-engineer.instruction: Configure the scripts that bring each station back online. Wrong sequence risks overloading the healthy grid. Arrange the steps.
software-engineer.hint: The backbone that feeds everything else comes first. Hospitals before homes. Test before you go full-scale.

items.label: Confirm every compromised station has been wiped clean
Bring back the main transmission stations that supply multiple zones
Run a test load to verify the backbone can handle demand
Restore district stations — hospitals and critical services first
Restore residential areas last, zone by zone

data-scientist.title: Find the Safe Restoration Speed
data-scientist.instruction: Restoring too fast can overload the lines and trigger another blackout. The graph shows what percentage of normal load the grid safely handled each hour during testing. How much can you safely restore in the next hour?
data-scientist.hint: The safe limit is growing each hour. Look at how much it grows between each hour and carry that pattern forward.

cloud-engineer.title: Secure Stations Before Restoring Power
cloud-engineer.instruction: Compromised control systems must be fully secured before going back online. 200,000 people are still without power, so time matters. What do you do?
cloud-engineer.hint: Speed matters because people are in the dark, but restoring a system that still has the attacker inside just hands them back control.

options.label: Complete rebuild from scratch — every device gets a fresh install. Takes 6 hours but you're 100% certain the attacker left no traces.
Surgically remove only the malicious parts found and close the gaps used. Done in 2 hours but 15% chance of missing something hidden.
Bring systems back under intense observation. If the attacker left anything, they'll reveal themselves when they try to act. Risky but gives the best picture.
Replace the physical equipment entirely. Most expensive, takes 12 hours, but eliminates any possibility of hidden threats surviving.
